URL: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/sep/24/tony-blair-britain-rejoin-eu-next-10-years-brexit
The Guardian — published Thu 24 September 2026 00:01 BST (2026-09-23T23:01:01Z) — Kiran Stacey

HEADLINE: Tony Blair says Britain should work towards rejoining EU in next 10 years
STANDFIRST: Andy Burnham under pressure to revisit Brexit as poll suggests pledge to rejoin could boost Labour's electoral chances

- Britain should work towards rejoining the EU in the next decade, Tony Blair has said, adding to growing pressure on Andy Burnham to abandon Labour's reluctance to revisit the 2016 referendum.
- The former prime minister has urged Burnham to use his 10-year plan in November to put the country's membership of the union back on the table, a decade after it voted to leave.
- In a paper entitled "A Path to Rejoining a Reformed Europe", the Tony Blair Institute (TBI) calls for the UK to accept free movement of people and make a financial contribution as the price of entry.
- The intervention comes after Burnham declined to rule out promising to rejoin the EU in the next Labour manifesto.

QUOTE — TONY BLAIR (foreword to the TBI paper): "Britain should signal an intention if the terms are right to enter into a structured formal relationship with Europe and initiate a process of negotiation where everything is on the table but nothing agreed until everything is agreed."

QUOTE — TBI researchers (in the paper): "Over the next decade, Britain should work towards the ambition of rejoining a significantly reformed EU."

QUOTE — ANDY BURNHAM (to reporters this week, when asked if rejoining could be in the next election manifesto): it was a question "for another day".

QUOTE — ANDY BURNHAM (to the Guardian last year): "I hope in my lifetime I see this country rejoin the European Union."

- Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, has called the Brexit vote a "catastrophic mistake" and said the party should aim to rejoin the bloc.
- Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, dismissed the idea earlier this year, warning against "reopening the circular arguments that we ended up in as a country".
- A new megapoll by YouGov for Best for Britain (13,000+ people, conducted in June, before Burnham became PM) suggests Labour could more than double its seat total if it went into the next election promising to rejoin — from a projected 136 seats to 321. Those totals will have changed since Burnham took office, which has given Labour a poll lead for the first time in months.
- The TBI paper says Burnham should scrap the government's red lines of not rejoining, not allowing free movement and not entering the single market or a customs union, replacing them with a single promise only to sign up to rules that prove of economic or strategic benefit to the UK.
- TBI funders include technology billionaire Larry Ellison; its clients include the government of Saudi Arabia.
